scope: Targeted primary-source review for the next part-3 stability hypothesis. No fitting, installation, existing-test tuning or production edits by this review.

recommended_single_hypothesis.name: User-separated cross-validated convex combination of two fixed final smoothers
recommended_single_hypothesis.question: Can observable held-out pseudo-outcome risk adapt the bias/variance tradeoff between the retained spline and an already fixed stronger local-linear smoother, improving stability across new cohorts?
library: Retained cubic smoothing spline with lambda_mean=1e-4 under the established scaling/loss convention
Previously fixed local-linear control with bandwidth multiplier 2 relative to its unchanged base bandwidth policy
recommended_single_hypothesis.change_only: Learn one convex mixing coefficient in [0,1] using whole-user held-out predictions, then shrink the LL2 contribution toward retained S using one development-selected gamma. Keep input, covariates, nuisance learners, GPS, pseudo-outcome formula, support and outcome units unchanged.
recommended_single_hypothesis.reason: This is a mature loss-based stacking adaptation that directly tests selection/stability rather than enlarging the prior lambda grid after seeing two adverse seeds.
recommended_single_hypothesis.condition_on_diagnosis: The parent diagnostic distinguishes reference-dose sampling residual in one adverse seed from other reference errors and error-cancellation cross terms in another. Do not force both into a single high-noise or incorrect-GPS explanation. The global mixture does not specifically correct reference-dose bias or identify its cause. It tests adaptive smoothing only; the actual diagnostic evidence and numbers are recorded by the separate audit, not recomputed here.
recommended_single_hypothesis.not_new: Not a new causal estimator, not a novel Super Learner, and not a full reproduction of the original Super Learner or BK experiments. It is a narrow task adaptation of established pseudo-outcome regression and validation-based aggregation.

primary_sources.title: Nonparametric methods for doubly robust estimation of continuous treatment effects
primary_sources.publication: JRSS Series B 79(4), 2017, 1229-1245; DOI 10.1111/rssb.12212. First preprint 2015, PDF examined v3 dated 2016-08-11.
primary_sources.evidence: Section 3.5, original PDF page 8: presents pseudo-outcome leave-one-out bandwidth selection, then explicitly describes k-fold validation that fits nuisance functions and effect curve on k-1 folds and computes risk on the remaining fold. It notes the additional cost and relevance for general machine learning.
primary_sources.interpretation: Supports a fully training-separated validation pipeline. It does not mean that splitting a globally precomputed pseudo-outcome table is exact end-to-end validation. Its original iid theory is not automatically a clustered-user theorem.

primary_sources.title: Fast convergence rates for dose-response estimation
primary_sources.dates: 2022 first arXiv; v2 revised 2026-04-12; author site lists EJS 2026.
primary_sources.evidence: Algorithm 1 and sections 2.1-2.2 support global ERM or linear-smoothing regression of DR pseudo-outcomes; smoothing splines are explicitly included. Independent construction samples and alternative splitting schemes are discussed.
primary_sources.interpretation: A small fixed library of final smoothers is methodologically reasonable. Higher-order influence-function correction or richer nuisance learners would be separate changes and are not part of this hypothesis.

primary_sources.title: Super learner
primary_sources.publication: Statistical Applications in Genetics and Molecular Biology 6, Article25, 2007; DOI 10.2202/1544-6115.1309.
primary_sources.evidence: Original abstract describes V-fold selection of weights combining a fixed initial learner library and generalization to parameters defined as loss minimizers.
primary_sources.interpretation: Established aggregation foundation, not a 2026 invention. Ordinary prediction oracle results do not directly certify this clustered estimated-response implementation or per-seed improvement.

primary_sources.implementation: Author implementation supports cross-validated risk, nonnegative normalized or convex least-squares combination methods, outer/inner validation controls, and an id variable keeping each cluster in one validation fold.
primary_sources.maintenance_evidence: Current author repository DESCRIPTION lists version 2.0-40 and package date 2025-12-14. Exact last commit date is not asserted.
primary_sources.limitation: Documentation explicitly notes that some learner wrappers ignore id or weights. Cluster-aware fold generation alone does not make a precomputed estimated outcome table correctly nested.
primary_sources.reuse_decision: Useful mature reference implementation, but do not install the R dependency stack for a two-column one-parameter convex least-squares problem. Independently implementing the elementary constrained formula in the existing Python runtime is lower cost. Do not present that as copying GPL code into the current module.

primary_sources.implementation: Lrnr_sl documents cluster_by_id and task-level id plus configurable validation structures; dependent units stay together.
primary_sources.maintenance_evidence: Current DESCRIPTION version 1.4.5; author organization listing showed sl3 updated 2025-07-07 and origami updated 2026-05-23. These are visible repository metadata, not evidence that this project's estimator was run.
primary_sources.decision: Alternative reference for correct clustered folds and nested validation, not an additional statistical candidate or installation requirement.

primary_sources.evidence: Official implementation offers GCV when lambda is omitted and an explicit regularization parameter otherwise; its loss is summed weighted squared residuals plus curvature penalty. The retained sample-size/amount-scaling conversion must remain unchanged when lambda_mean=1e-4 is passed to its summed-loss implementation.
primary_sources.license: BSD-3-Clause verified in the preceding targeted review.
primary_sources.decision: Keep the previous explicit fixed lambda policy inside the two-member library. Ordinary GCV is not a ready-made user-cluster validation method; adding it now would be an expanded library and another hypothesis.

correct_feasible_selection_pipeline.status: Proposed, not executed by this review
correct_feasible_selection_pipeline.folds: A small fixed number of whole-user folds, declared before new development scoring. Three folds is a feasible initial budget; it is a design choice, not a literature-mandated optimum.
per_fold: Let V be all events of held-out users and T the other users. V outcomes may not enter any model used to produce either candidate's prediction at V amounts.

Within T alone, run the existing user-cross-fitting nuisance pipeline to construct training pseudo-outcomes xi_T. All nuisance models used for xi_T must be fitted using T users only. Fit the two final smoothers on these xi_T values.

Fit the unchanged nuisance specifications using T alone to evaluate xi_V. The outcome marginalization/empirical covariate average and marginal treatment density used for xi_V must use training data only under the declared target. Do not use V outcomes or a global-data-trained nuisance object.

Predict both T-trained final curves at the held-out observed amounts A_V in the predeclared selection interval [0.3,2.1] and save their predictions with xi_V. This interval restriction is fixed before new development. Use the same support scoring policy for both; record unsupported folds/amounts rather than silently dropping one candidate's failures.
Repeat across folds, then choose a single convex weight from the held-out predictions using the predefined user-weighted squared loss. No true simulator curve enters this weight calculation.

For the final dataset estimator, reconstruct the existing full-data user-cross-fitted xi, fit the same two fixed final smoothers, and use the learned mixture coefficient. Evaluate its contrast as the mixture curve at a minus the same mixture curve at a0.
correct_feasible_selection_pipeline.leakage_counterexample: A globally OOF xi table only excludes each row's own nuisance fold. When a second GroupKFold is later applied, xi values of training users can have been built by nuisances trained on the new validation users' outcomes. Thus merely GroupKFold-splitting that table is not strictly training-separated pipeline validation.
correct_feasible_selection_pipeline.outer_assessment: The held-out predictions used to learn the mixture weight are training data for that meta-parameter. Their optimized risk is not an unbiased assessment of the fitted ensemble. Use the genuinely new fixed final cohort for final performance; use another outer loop only if an unbiased internal performance estimate is actually needed.
correct_feasible_selection_pipeline.cost: Additional fold-restricted nuisance fits are required; final-smoother computations alone cannot remove dependence already embedded in cached xi. Cache training-only objects within each fold so both fixed smoothers share every nuisance fit. No runtime measured here.

formula_code_contract.candidate: Convention: alpha is the S weight. f_alpha(a)=alpha*f_spline(a)+(1-alpha)*f_LL2(a), with 0<=alpha<=1. Thus alpha=1 exactly recovers retained S.
formula_code_contract.weight_objective: Minimize sum_i w_i*(xi_V_i - b_i - alpha*d_i)^2 over alpha in [0,1] on the fixed observed-amount interval [0.3,2.1], where b_i=f_LL2,T(A_i) and d_i=f_spline,T(A_i)-b_i.
formula_code_contract.closed_form: alpha_CV=clip(sum_i w_i*d_i*(xi_V_i-b_i) / sum_i w_i*d_i^2, 0, 1). If the two prediction columns coincide exactly, their mixtures coincide and the prespecified retained-S tie alpha=1 is valid.
formula_code_contract.task_regularization: alpha_eff=1-gamma*(1-alpha_CV), gamma in the fixed development grid [0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1]. gamma=0 recovers S and gamma=1 uses the unshrunk CV mixture. This equation is specific to alpha being the S weight; reversing alpha requires changing the equation.
formula_code_contract.constant_mixture_control: f_beta(a)=beta*S(a)+(1-beta)*LL2(a), beta in [0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1]. Both the adaptive-gamma policy and this constant-beta control get five development choices; freeze one gamma and one beta before confirmation.
formula_code_contract.regularization_claim: The gamma shrinkage strategy and five-choice constant control are task adaptations. Super Learner supports loss-based convex aggregation, but no cited paper is claimed to prove a theorem for this exact gamma policy or guarantee its improvement. Beating S alone cannot establish that data adaptation caused the gain; compare with the frozen constant-mixture control.
formula_code_contract.weights: For a user-targeted risk, each user's total weight is equal and events divide that user's weight. With exactly two events per user this equals ordinary event-averaged loss up to a constant. Preserve the declared target if event counts later differ.
formula_code_contract.same_estimator: Using a single global convex coefficient preserves smoothness and differentiability inherited from each base curve. Do not make alpha a dose-dependent gating function in this pilot.
formula_code_contract.bounds: Neither DR pseudo-outcomes nor contrasts are clipped merely because observed Y is bounded. No new GPS clipping, response filtering or support override.
formula_code_contract.fixed_library: Keep spline lambda_mean=1e-4 and the already declared LL bandwidth multiplier 2; the multiplier is applied to the same bandwidth policy at each fold's training size. Original LL multiplier 1 can remain a reporting baseline but is not an extra ensemble member. No richer GPS, outcome learner changes, extra spline lambdas, additional bandwidth searches, derivative fitting changes or hidden-confounding claims in this comparison.

important_statistical_limits: The conditional mean of a nuisance-estimated validation xi can differ from theta(A) by nuisance bias b(A). Expected xi squared loss equals a candidate-independent conditional variance term plus squared loss against theta+b. Validation reduces selection leakage but cannot remove that bias.

In finite samples xi noise need not cancel when comparing learners. Large inverse-density residuals can make the learned coefficient unstable. Diagnose user-level risk contributions and signal scales; do not trim users or replace squared loss with Huber silently because doing so changes the procedure/target.

The convex library contains the retained spline at alpha=1, but does not guarantee better future risk or no seed regressions after estimating alpha. Finite-sample selection may choose poorly. Greater disagreement between S and LL2 makes alpha estimable but does not establish that LL2 is useful.

Risk at observed validation amounts weights the treatment distribution. Uniform evaluation-grid error and fixed-reference contrast error are different objectives. Treat the latter as independent outcome checks, not as theoretically optimized by ordinary squared level risk.

For error e(a)=f_hat(a)-theta(a), contrast error is e(a)-e(a0). Better overall level risk can coexist with larger contrast error if reference-point error or its covariance changes. Do not infer reference contrast success solely from reduced level risk.
Correct user separation is an operational adaptation; no iid Super Learner/BK oracle theorem is claimed as a ready-made guarantee for repeated events and fitted pseudo-outcomes.
A lack of overlap or hidden confounding is an identification problem; mixing two curves fitted to the same biased xi cannot repair it.

new_data_comparison_proposal.role_of_old_seeds: The two adverse seeds 90342003 and 90342005 are diagnosis/development evidence only. Do not choose alpha, alter lambda, tune risk weights, or report a fresh confirmation by optimizing their true curves.
new_data_comparison_proposal.development: Parent-proposed fixed plan, not generated by this literature task: 4 new seed blocks times 6 mechanisms to select gamma and constant beta once. Declare the S(lambda_mean=1e-4)/LL2 two-member library, [0.3,2.1] selection interval and exact nested user-split procedure beforehand. LL2's earlier control role and old-seed diagnosis motivate the hypothesis, not independent evidence of benefit. Inspect alpha_CV and risk/contrast alignment. The 24 mechanism curves still contain only 4 independent seed blocks.
new_data_comparison_proposal.confirmation_plan: Parent-proposed fixed plan: after gamma/beta freeze, 12 new seed blocks times 8 mechanisms. These 96 mechanism curves contain 12 seed blocks; score paired per-seed changes rather than claiming 96 independent randomized replications. Primary score remains uniform-grid reference-contrast RMSE; observed-dose level risk only estimates the within-dataset mixing weight.
new_data_comparison_proposal.single_next_step: If diagnosis supports smoother instability and the fresh development comparison is useful, freeze this one procedure and assess it once on new fixed seeds/mechanisms. If not useful, retain the current method and record why rather than enlarge the library using the same final truth.
metrics: Primary: same reference-contrast RMSE and full-range output rate as the previous accepted comparison.
Separately: level RMSE, reference error, per-seed/per-mechanism contrast change, maximum curve error, alpha distribution and user-level held-out risk contributions.
Derivative and crossing errors remain distinct secondary outcomes; no whole-chain claim from the primary mean-curve result.
new_data_comparison_proposal.numerical_claims: No new effect-size, improvement percentage, accuracy or runtime result generated in this literature-only task.
